observed: Full English keyboard campaign on the frozen source won for 1800 points: all three summits (Moonlit Atrium, Cable Gallery, Broken Spire) and all scoring ledges. X at braziers refilled the lamp each time; moving cable decks carried the climber.

The required Broken Spire rail was climbed with Z+Up (stamina 100 to 82) and exited with Left+Space while Z was still held, landing on the high ledge for 1400. Releasing Z on the same frame as Space detaches instead of jumping, which matches the help text.

Two real falls from the rail section each cost one life and returned the climber to the summit-2 brazier with full grip and unchanged score; a short walk-off onto a lower ledge cost nothing. The run finished with 2 of 4 lives because of these tester timing mistakes.

Pause while gripping preserved stamina 91 and the climbing state on resume. The shared host clears held input on every pause/resume (src/app.js); physical keys return through auto-repeat, so the tester re-pressed Z after resuming.

Lamp exhaustion alone cost a life about every 70 seconds and reached the explicit loss at about 270 seconds with score 400. Arrow, X and Z+Up input on the loss screen left status, score and best unchanged. R restarted at score 0 with best 1800.

Chinese 390x844 portrait: no horizontal overflow, readable canvas HUD, all seven touch controls; touch Refill restored the lamp 51 to 100 and two multi-touch direction+jump presses scored 200. 844x390 landscape fullscreen places controls in side columns; touch jumps scored to 400.
limitations: Headless Chrome with emulated phone layouts and dispatched touch events; no physical device or audio check.
After the win, Space activated the focused Play Again button (host behavior), so terminal freeze was checked on the loss screen with non-activating keys.

finalBrowser: Installed stable Google Chrome 156.0.8078.80 (headless, temporary profile) driven over the DevTools protocol from a parent script. The Codex Chrome extension and Claude in Chrome were unavailable in the continuation session. Only trusted keyboard, mouse and touch input events were dispatched; visible DOM text and screenshots were read; no game state was read or injected and Playwright was not used.
